fields.name: The Hilbert-Smith Conjecture
fields.statement: Hilbert's fifth problem asked how far differentiability can be removed from the theory of continuous transformation groups. Gleason, Montgomery-Zippin and Yamabe settled the case of locally Euclidean groups. The Hilbert-Smith conjecture asks about groups acting on manifolds: if a locally compact group $G$ acts faithfully and continuously on a connected topological manifold $M$, must $G$ be a Lie group? Equivalently, can the $p$-adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_p$ act faithfully on a manifold? It was known in dimensions at most 2, in dimension 3 (Pardon 2013), and for Lipschitz, quasiconformal and some Holder actions. Is every such group a Lie group, in every dimension?

fields.name: Simon's Problem 2: pure-point spectrum for the two-dimensional Anderson model at every disorder
fields.statement: Let $H=\Delta+v$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2)$, with nearest-neighbor hopping and independent site potentials $v_x$ uniform on $[-h,h]$. The scaling theory of Abrahams, Anderson, Licciardello and Ramakrishnan (1979) predicts no metallic behavior in two dimensions, at any disorder. Rigorous localization was known only at large disorder or at extreme energies (Frohlich-Spencer, Frohlich-Martinelli-Scoppola-Spencer, Aizenman-Molchanov) and near the band edge (Ding-Smart). Simon's Problem 2 asks: for every $h>0$, does $H$ almost surely have pure-point spectrum throughout its spectrum?

fields.statement: Let $H_\lambda=-\Delta+\lambda V$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ with iid site potentials $V_x$ uniform on $[-1,1]$. fields.name: The Baum-Connes Conjecture (coefficient-free, reduced)
fields.statement: For a countable discrete group $G$, the Baum-Connes assembly map $\mu^G:K_*^G(\underline{E}G)\to K_*(C_r^*(G))$ sends equivariant $K$-homology of the classifying space for proper actions to the $K$-theory of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra. Baum and Connes conjectured that it is an isomorphism. It was proved for a-T-menable groups (Higson-Kasparov) and hyperbolic groups (Mineyev-Yu, Lafforgue); Higson-Lafforgue-Skandalis disproved the version with coefficients, but the coefficient-free group conjecture stayed open. Is $\mu^G$ an isomorphism for every countable discrete group $G$?

Maximal assembly and the classical Novikov conjecture are not disproved.
fields.resultNote: Three counterexamples. (1) A finitely generated group with a projection in $C_r^*(G)$ of irrational canonical trace, so $\mu_0^G$ is not surjective. (2) A finitely generated torsion-free group whose degree-zero reduced assembly map kills a class of infinite order, so rational injectivity fails (the reduced form of the strong Novikov conjecture). (3) The Kadison-Kaplansky counterexample also gives a torsion-free group with a class outside the assembly image. Not shown: failure of maximal assembly, a finitely presented counterexample, or failure of the classical Novikov conjecture.

fields.name: The Kadison-Kaplansky Projection Conjecture
fields.statement: For a torsion-free discrete group $H$, let $C_r^*(H)$ be its reduced group $C^*$-algebra. Pimsner and Voiculescu proved it for free groups, and it follows from surjectivity of the coefficient-free Baum-Connes map, so it holds for amenable and hyperbolic groups. fields.name: Bloch's Conjecture for Surfaces with $p_g=0$
fields.statement: For a smooth connected projective complex surface $S$, the Albanese map $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\mathrm{Alb}(S)(\mathbb{C})$ on degree-zero zero-cycles modulo rational equivalence is surjective. fields.name: The Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
fields.shortName: Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
fields.field: Algebraic geometry: Hodge theory and algebraic cycles on abelian varieties
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex variety. The rational Hodge conjecture asserts that every class in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb Q)\cap H^{p,p}(X)$ is a rational linear combination of classes of codimension-$p$ algebraic subvarieties. For abelian varieties it is known in codimension one (Lefschetz) and in scattered cases; Deligne proved every Hodge class on an abelian variety is absolute Hodge, and Deligne and Andre reduced Hodge classes on CM abelian varieties to Weil-type classes on auxiliary CM varieties, without producing the cycles. Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety with complex multiplication, so that $\mathrm{End}(A)\otimes\mathbb Q$ contains a commutative semisimple algebra of dimension $2\dim A$. Is every rational Hodge class on $A$, in every codimension, algebraic?

fields.field: Arithmetic geometry: algebraic cycles and l-adic cohomology
fields.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, $\bar A$ its base change to $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$, and $\ell$ a prime different from the characteristic. The Tate conjecture predicts that the $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb F}_q/\mathbb F_q)$-invariant classes in $H^{2r}_{et}(\bar A,\mathbb Q_\ell(r))$ are spanned by classes of algebraic cycles defined over $\mathbb F_q$, and that numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree. It is known for divisors (Tate) and in some further cases. Milne proved in 1999 that the Hodge conjecture for complex CM abelian varieties would imply it for all abelian varieties over finite fields. fields.name: The amenability problem for Thompson's group F (Geoghegan's conjecture)
fields.statement: Thompson's group $F$ is the group, under composition, of increasing piecewise linear homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$ with finitely many pieces, dyadic rational breakpoints and slopes in $2^{\mathbb Z}$. fields.name: The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions
fields.statement: For $\omega\in S^2$ and $0<\delta<1$ let $K_\delta f(\omega)$ be the supremum, over unit tubes of radius $\delta$ in direction $\omega$, of the average of $|f|$ on the tube. fields.name: The Fourier restriction conjecture in three dimensions for positively curved surfaces: bounded-data and diagonal forms
fields.statement: For a compact smooth positively curved surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, such as the sphere, let $E_\Sigma f(x)=\int_\Sigma f(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\sigma(\xi)$. fields.name: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis: a fixed zero-free half-plane for zeta and all Dirichlet L-functions
fields.statement: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis asks for one gap that works at every height: is there a fixed $\sigma_0<1$ such that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>\sigma_0$? fields.name: The Landau-Siegel zero problem: a uniform logarithmic gap for real zeros of real Dirichlet L-functions
fields.statement: For a primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q$, the classical zero-free region $\Re s\ge1-c_1/\log(q(|\Im s|+2))$ holds with one possible exception: a single simple real zero $\beta$ attached to a real character, which could lie very close to $1$. fields.name: Vinogradov's least quadratic nonresidue conjecture
fields.statement: For an odd prime $p$, let $n(p)$ be the least positive integer that is a quadratic nonresidue modulo $p$. fields.name: Derandomization of logarithmic space: is L = RL = BPL?
fields.statement: $\mathsf L$ is the class of languages decided in deterministic logarithmic space. $\mathsf{RL}$ allows a polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine fresh random bits with one-sided error (acceptance probability $0$ on no-inputs, at least $1/2$ on yes-inputs), and $\mathsf{BPL}$ allows two-sided bounded error ($\le1/3$ versus $\ge2/3$). Aleliunas, Karp, Lipton, Lovasz and Rackoff, after giving a randomized logspace algorithm for undirected connectivity, asked whether polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space can be simulated in deterministic logarithmic space. The best unconditional results before this work were Saks-Zhou space $O(\log^{3/2}n)$, improved by Hoza to $O(\log^{3/2}n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$, and Nisan's simultaneous polynomial time with $O(\log^2n)$ space. fields.statement: If $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ satisfies $\sum_{n\in A}1/n=\infty$, must $A$ contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions? fields.name: Global classical solutions of the 3D relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system for large data
fields.statement: The relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system couples a particle density $f(t,x,v)\ge0$ on $\mathbb R^3_x\times\mathbb R^3_v$, transported by $\partial_tf+\hat v\cdot\nabla_xf+(E+\hat v\times B)\cdot\nabla_vf=0$ with $\hat v=v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}$, to Maxwell's equations with charge and current densities computed from $f$. Wollman proved local existence of classical solutions, DiPerna and Lions global weak solutions, and Glassey and Strauss showed that a classical solution continues as long as its momentum support stays bounded and proved global existence for small (dilute) data. Global classical existence was known only under smallness, symmetry or reduced dimension. For arbitrary smooth, compactly supported particle data and smooth finite-energy fields satisfying the constraints, does the classical solution exist for all time?

fields.name: The blockwise Alperin weight conjecture
fields.field: Modular representation theory of finite groups
fields.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and $G$ a finite group. A $p$-weight of $G$ is a pair $(Q,\phi)$ with $Q$ a $p$-subgroup and $\phi$ an irreducible character of $N_G(Q)/Q$ of $p$-defect zero; each weight is assigned to a $p$-block of $G$ by Brauer induction. For a block $B$, let $l(B)$ be the number of irreducible Brauer characters (simple modules) in $B$ and let $W_p(B)$ be the set of $G$-conjugacy classes of weights assigned to $B$. Alperin conjectured that simple modules are counted locally, block by block. Does $l(B)=|W_p(B)|$ hold for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every $p$-block $B$?

fields.name: The Unique Games Conjecture
fields.statement: A Unique Games instance is a graph with a finite label set $K$ and, on each edge, a permutation of $K$; a labeling satisfies an edge when the label at one endpoint is the image of the other endpoint's label under that permutation. fields.name: Hadwiger's Conjecture
fields.statement: For a graph $G$ let $h(G)$, the Hadwiger number, be the largest $t$ such that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$. It was known for $t\le5$ (Hadwiger and Dirac for $t=3$, Wagner plus the Four Colour Theorem for $t=4$, Robertson-Seymour-Thomas for $t=5$). The special case of graphs with independence number at most two (equivalently, every such $m$-vertex graph has a $K_{\lceil m/2\rceil}$ minor, Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft) and the fractional weakening $\chi_f(G)\le h(G)$ discussed by Reed and Seymour (1998) were also open. fields.name: The Colin de Verdiere Chromatic Conjecture
fields.statement: Colin de Verdiere (1990) introduced the graph invariant $\mu(G)$: the maximum nullity of a real symmetric matrix that is negative on edges, zero on non-edges, has exactly one negative eigenvalue and satisfies the Strong Arnold Property. fields.name: The Linear List Hadwiger Conjecture
fields.statement: Kawarabayashi and Mohar (2007, Conjecture 1.3) proposed a linear relaxation of Hadwiger's conjecture for list colouring: there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every graph with no $K_t$ minor is $Ct$-choosable. Degeneracy gives $O(t\sqrt{\log t})$; the best list bounds before this work were superlinear (for example Postle's $O(t(\log\log t)^6)$), and $K_t$-minor-free graphs can have list chromatic number close to $2t$, so $C=1$ is impossible. Even the ordinary-colouring version, $\chi(G)=O(h(G))$, was open. Is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\chi_\ell(G)\le C\,h(G)$ for every graph $G$?

fields.statement: A connected matching in a graph is a matching whose edges are pairwise joined by at least one edge. fields.name: Cannon's Conjecture
fields.statement: Let $G$ be a word-hyperbolic group whose Gromov boundary $\partial G$ is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere. Cannon's conjecture, stated by Cannon and Swenson (1998, Conjecture 5.1), asserts that $G$ acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb H^3$; for torsion-free $G$ this would make $G$ the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold. Cannon-Floyd-Parry reduced it to bounds on discrete annular moduli, and Bonk-Kleiner proved it when the Ahlfors regular conformal dimension of the boundary is attained. Does every hyperbolic group with boundary $S^2$ act geometrically on $\mathbb H^3$?

fields.name: Artin's Primitive Root Conjecture: Infinitude for Every Admissible Base
fields.shortName: Artin's conjecture: infinitude for every base
fields.statement: Artin conjectured in 1927 that every integer $a\ne-1$ that is not a perfect square is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes $p$, and more precisely that the number of such $p\le x$ is asymptotic to $A(a)\,x/\log x$ for an explicit constant $A(a)>0$. Hooley (1967) proved this under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Kummer fields. Unconditionally, Gupta-Murty and Heath-Brown (1986) showed that at most two prime bases fail the infinitude assertion, so one of $2,3,5$ works, but no single prescribed base such as $a=2$ was known to be a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Is every admissible integer $a$ a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, with the predicted density?

It does not give the predicted asymptotic $A(a)\,x/\log x$: the count is short by a factor $\log x$ and constants depend on $a$. The companion on simultaneous primitive roots gives the same lower bound for any finite set of prime bases, assuming four inputs from this paper.

fields.name: Kadison's Similarity Problem
fields.statement: Kadison (1955) asked whether every bounded unital homomorphism $\pi$ from a unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ into the bounded operators $B(H)$ on a Hilbert space is similar to a $*$-homomorphism, that is, whether there is a bounded invertible $S$ such that $S\pi(\cdot)S^{-1}$ is a $*$-homomorphism. Known cases included nuclear algebras (Bunce, Christensen), cyclic representations and algebras without tracial states (Haagerup) and II$_1$ factors with property $\Gamma$ (Christensen). Haagerup showed similarity is equivalent to complete boundedness, and Kirchberg showed the problem is equivalent to the derivation problem. Is every bounded representation of a $C^*$-algebra on Hilbert space similar to a $*$-representation?
